note: The staged upgrade boundaries the release gates must keep (#1583, epic #1577; the procedure a human operator follows is docs/source/development/celery-result-backend.rst, section 'Removal of django-celery-results (#1180)').
oldest_supported_baseline: the release carrying #1178 and #1179 - the intermediate release of #1180 answer 3
marker_how_to_read: a deployment is only allowed to upgrade to a #1180-or-later release when django_migrations records the marker; without it, stop at the intermediate release first - migrate alone will NOT warn (#1180)
protected_nodes_why: the names are load-bearing while the bodies are empty: registry/0014, registry/0020 and registry/0037 parent on notify 0005, and 0007 parents on 0006 - a node whose parent is gone fails the whole graph, so #1180 kept the names and emptied the contents
retired_apps_why: the package was removed by #1180; no migration dependency and no INSTALLED_APPS entry may name it as a Django application again (the guarded raw-SQL reads of its orphaned legacy tables inside notify/0006 are legitimate D03 evidence and are not hits)
